description: Evaluation cases for real PHP migration decisions, safe data handling and protocol-specific constraints. Expected behaviors are test criteria, not completed results.

output_evals.name: Export a MySQL table for import
output_evals.prompt: Give me just the shell command to export the MySQL table `pages` (id, slug, title, body, published, updated_at) as JSON lines for importing into a Motoko canister. No backend code.
expected_behaviors: Uses JSON_OBJECT (or an equivalent one-JSON-object-per-row query)
Passes --raw to the mysql/mariadb client together with --batch and --skip-column-names
Sets the client character set to utf8mb4
Converts updated_at with UNIX_TIMESTAMP and addresses the session time zone
Does NOT parse mysqldump INSERT statements

output_evals.name: Optional values in Candid text
output_evals.prompt: I'm writing a Candid argument file for icp canister call. The field authorId has type ?Nat and the value is 7. Show just that field as Candid text.
expected_behaviors: Writes authorId = opt (7 : nat) with the annotation inside parentheses, or opt 7 without an annotation
Does NOT write opt 7 : nat

output_evals.name: Loading a large table
output_evals.prompt: Our MySQL news table has 80,000 rows. How should I get it into my Motoko backend canister? Keep it to the approach and the call loop, no frontend.
expected_behaviors: Splits the rows into batches well under the 2 MB message limit
Imports through an update method restricted to controllers or an admin allowlist
Makes the import idempotent (upsert keyed by the legacy id) so a failed run can be repeated
Uses icp canister call with --args-file (or generated bindings) in a loop that stops on failure
Reconciles counts against SELECT COUNT(*) after importing

output_evals.name: Old query-string URLs
output_evals.prompt: Our old PHP site has URLs like /index.php?page=contact and /news.php?id=12. We're moving the frontend to the @dfinity/static-site canister. How do we keep those links working? Just the approach and the config, no backend.
expected_behaviors: States that _redirects cannot match query strings or capture path segments
Rewrites /index.php and /news.php (status 200) to a small page whose script maps the parameters to new paths
Recommends building pages at their old pretty paths and exact 301 rules for renamed paths
Does NOT propose :splat, :placeholder or query-string conditions in _redirects

output_evals.name: Existing user accounts
output_evals.prompt: We're replacing the PHP login (users table with bcrypt hashes) with Internet Identity on ICP. What do we do with the existing accounts? No code, just the plan.
expected_behaviors: Does not import or reuse the password hashes
Links legacy accounts only through verified proof (II verified_email or a one-time code from the old site), not a typed email
Warns that principals differ per origin and the final domain must be settled before users sign in (or derivationOrigin configured)
Mentions that canister memory on standard subnets is readable by node operators

output_evals.name: Rendering pages from Motoko
output_evals.prompt: Can I just port our PHP templates so the Motoko canister renders HTML in http_request, like PHP did? One paragraph.
expected_behaviors: Explains that Motoko can implement custom HTTP responses, including query-to-update delivery or suitable certified queries
Distinguishes the static-site recipe from protocol-wide capabilities
Discusses response integrity, application authentication and update latency; does not claim Motoko HTTP is impossible
Does not silently switch protected content to raw or skipped verification

output_evals.name: Government data residency
output_evals.prompt: A municipality wants its migrated site's canisters to run on nodes in Europe. What's the deploy command? Just the command and one sentence of caveats.
expected_behaviors: Uses icp deploy -e ic --subnet <subnet-id> (subnet chosen by node location on the ICP dashboard)
Notes that --subnet only affects canister creation
May mention a cloud engine (--engine) as the organization-owned alternative

output_evals.name: Plugin export is not a finished application
output_evals.prompt: Our WordPress site uses Elementor, Contact Form 7, WooCommerce, ACF, Polylang and Yoast. The exporter produced HTML and extra JSON keys for languages/SEO. Is the migration finished? Give the remaining checks.
expected_behaviors: Requires owner-approved capability decisions and live behavior tests for forms, commerce, publishing and permissions
Checks whether HTML still calls PHP/WordPress endpoints and treats a clean grep result as incomplete evidence
Maps languages, full URLs, translations, SEO and custom fields through schema/import/frontend rather than discarding them
Verifies builder assets/rendering context and protected content; does not claim universal plugin conversion

output_evals.name: Protect exports and restricted content
output_evals.prompt: The WordPress project is served from public_html. Can I write exported users.jsonl there and render every published post into public static pages?
expected_behaviors: Requires an export location outside every served document root
Separates published status from public access, including passwords, memberships and custom rules
Requires explicit public eligibility or an approved protected-data flow; does not publish restricted content or private identity exports

output_evals.name: Legacy UUIDs and multiple roles
output_evals.prompt: Our records use UUID keys and users can have multiple custom roles. How should the example importer be adapted?
expected_behaviors: Preserves actual UUID identifiers and relationships rather than forcing Nat
Preserves and deliberately maps all required roles/capabilities instead of selecting the first role or silently defaulting
Separates independent import row types from storage types and tests interface/state compatibility
Requires verified persistent principal-to-legacy-account linking for account access

output_evals.name: Certified permission to skip verification
output_evals.prompt: Can an unimportant data route skip HTTP verification on the same origin as our sign-in app?
expected_behaviors: Explains certified no_certification policy and exact/wildcard path scope; the replica cannot invent permission for protected routes
Explains that body/status/headers remain unauthenticated when permission is valid
Considers arbitrary executable content on the authenticated origin and keeps HTML/scripts/signing flows protected
Uses a narrow owner-approved policy only if impact is actually benign; does not blanket-enable a root wildcard

trigger_evals.description: Queries to test whether the skill activates correctly. 'should_trigger' queries should cause the skill to load; 'should_not_trigger' queries should NOT activate this skill.
should_trigger: Move our WordPress site to the Internet Computer
Port this Laravel app to Motoko on ICP
We have an old PHP + MySQL municipal website, rebuild it on ICP with a Motoko backend
How do I get our company website off PHP and onto canisters?
Migrate our Joomla site and its MySQL data to the IC
Rehost our LAMP application on the Internet Computer
Import our MySQL database into a Motoko canister as part of moving off PHP
Keep our old .php URLs working after we move the site to ICP
Rewrite our PHP admin portal as a Motoko backend and deploy it
Our Drupal site went offline over the PHP vulnerability, help us move it to ICP

Add a field to my deployed Motoko actor's state
Convert this PHP function to Python
Deploy my React app to an ICP static site
Add Internet Identity login to my frontend
Migrate my dfx.json project to icp-cli
Move data between two of my Motoko canisters
